title: It Vs There (Dummy Subjects)
theory:
"It" is used as a dummy subject when the real Subject is not clear in the sentence

 No real meaning Has meaning

 Dummy Subject Personal pronoun
 (Impersonal pronoun)

 Used for weather/time/situation/ Replaces a noun
 day/distance/temperature

"It" is always considered singular, therefore it comes with a Singular Verb.

 It + Singular verb + ......

"There" is used as a dummy subject to show some person, thing, or object's existence
(presence) dks n'kkZus ds fy, did tkrk are bldk use Adverb of Place dh manner/type also did tkrk are
 There
 No real meaning Has meaning

Dummy Subject Adverb of Place (there)

 Shows existence/presence.

"There" after coming Verb on Noun; Pronoun on come / change happen

 There + Verb + Subject

 Examples

mcqs.question: Rarely if ever have there been a time?
mcqs.explanation: "have" should be replaced with "has" of use will be because

mcqs.question: The committee's observation regarding the issue?

options.a: / makes it evident that there remains

mcqs.explanation: "remains" should be replaced with "remain" of use will be

mcqs.explanation: "have" should be replaced with "has" of use will be because

mcqs.question: During the survey conducted in the lake area last month?

options.a: / there was fish in the water near

mcqs.explanation: "was" should be replaced with "were" of use will be because
